reviews.text: We had the opportunity to visit one of Yunnan's wonder.. Lets dive in! Tiger Leaping Gorge, with many variations of folklore, is actually an amazing place to visit. If you are one to think about losing weight, here is where you can do so while having a scene like those out from a painting. The how part to lose weight is to constantly go along gorge up and down repeatedly..heheh.. Nonetheless, avid photographers, this is one place to go to. We got some nice shots, thus so can you. We actually also chanced upon a cafe at the end. Thus the we decided to stop to get our coffee fix🎉.. E Moment was a life saver. From the views they had to overlook the gorge, to the coffee we needed, this is definitely the place to be at. All in all, we would highly recommend to visit.. but come by the late aftenoon, with lesser of the crowd but dont take our word for it. Crowd could come at anytime, jz that we were glad we didnt have to handle much crowd on site. Check out our images for E Moment and decide for yourself the need to stop. Cheers!

"Tiger 🐅 Leaping Gorge" is a name of a very famous gorge in Yunnan province, China. You'll see beautiful and stunning high altitude scenery, dramatic rapids and roaring currents. Wonderful experience.

Suggest go on early and last winter, great landscapes, a little crowd if u want to take photos. Must wear layers of clothes! There are 2 elevators to go up and down, go down 35, go up 65, buy online will be cheaper. Very low oxygen, u could ready for some situation, u can also buy oxygen bottle before go down. The path is as high as 10 floors walk. Have bathrooms. If u lucky, u can see some squirrels. Have a good day!

Park ur car, buy ticket 4d bus ride thn buy ticket for escalator 70y unless u want to walk down, i hv a knee problem so escalator here v come. Once at the bottom u get push to take another tourist trap of foto which is ofcos optional when u get out. Thy actually laminate the foto 4u which is a good thing. Tiger leaping gorge changes base on which season u visit, winter the water average but when the snow melts there’s a lot more water going thru dat gorge thn it wld b magnificent even scary but dats pretty much it.

Magnificent scenic tour. Different part of the year has different views and experience. For those who are unable to do stairs, you have to pay for the escalator service. its worth it because its a long way down and up. Wind is really strong so warm clothes are definitely required.

Shangri-la Hutiaoxia Scenic is just beside Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. It's well built and easy to walk on the way to see the tiger symbolize. The river flows hard and strong. All the visitors must be alerted to the handphones and devices that may fall down. The atmosphere here is freezing and cold. The air pollution is Nice and comfortable breezes. Worth coming to have a visit but once in a lifetime is enough.

We reached Tiger Leaping Gorge, not too far from Lijiang. Many people include it when visiting Lijiang, but it’s actually located in the Shangri-La region. The dramatic views of the gorge were powerful and impressive.

One sight stop filled with amenities (coffee, souvenirs, the north face, dumplings and toilets). Multiple platforms and escalators. If you’re looking to hike Tiger Leaping Gorge, do not make the mistake of taking a bus to lower gorge scenic spot, as the trail head (upper gorge) is not walkable from this point. Our bus driver attempted to sell us extra packages to bring us to middle gorge (by taxi or bus). There really isn’t much to do unless you’re planning to pay a Taxi to drive you to a trail head. If you’re an experience hiker / backcountry camper (think Rockies, Alps, Patagonia), Tiger leaping gorge is underwhelming and very easily could be skipped all together.

It was a joyful day climbing down the numerous stairway to the bottom level no sweat, however coming back up to the street level by foot was phenominal, and it started to rain when we started to climb our way up with no umbrella. There was no elevator at all during that period of time.

Tiger Leaping Gorge is absolutely stunning and full of natural power. The river rushes through the narrow valley with incredible force—it’s truly astonishing to see up close. Surrounded by steep cliffs and dramatic scenery, this place perfectly shows the wild beauty of Yunnan. A must-visit for nature lovers and photographers.

This spot is a must-see! The views of the mountains and (aggressive) river stream are really incredible. The one caveat is that climbing up the stairs after you're done sightseeing can be brutal if you're not used to physical activity. They have a lot of benches along the climb back up for resting or you can buy an escalator package to save the energy
The view is nice but overly touristy. For guys, do visit the public toilet as there is better view than the shots I’ve captured.
Wonderful place with good location for take a photo. Nice weather. I been here in early of Oct. temperature around 20-25. Crowed with tourist.

This is a Large natural gorge, one of the deepest in the world! Reconmended to pay escalator fees of RMB70 both way. But, u still need to climb 200 staircase down/up! Not wheelchair friendly. If you don't have energy to climb staircase, not Reconmended. The toilet also not in good condition. It is tourist spot, hope local authorities can take some action.

This is a hiking place but even if you do not wish to hike , you can still take a public bus from “Lijiang passenger transport terminal” to the entrance to take amazing photos of the Tiger statue & the gushing river! Further, you can arrange for private car transport to go to Tea Horse guesthouse and see the million dollar view of Jade Dragon snow mountain right in front of you ! If you choose to hike , the full hike would require you to first go to 纳西雅阁 Naxi guesthouse , the starting point , to hike the challenging upslope “28 bends” and reach Tea Horse guesthouse / Halfway guesthouse to stay the night, before continuing on to either 1) Tina’s guesthouse to buy tickets to take the public bus to go back Lijiang / Shangri-La or 2) Teacher Zhang’s guesthouse to arrange for private car pick up to go back Lijiang / Shangri-La For half day hike, you would have to arrange private car transport to either Tea Horse / Halfway guesthouse and then hike the rest of the way to either Tina’s or Teacher Zhang guesthouse. Do note some parts of the hike after the waterfall are difficult and you need to be careful. Note: When I visited , many of the scenic spots in the middle of the gorge such as the Gorge rock & 168 sky ladder were closed due to reports of accidents, hopefully they will open again soon… Overall, the scenery is as authentic as you can get and the view of the gushing river and mountain is truly spectacular !

Absolutely beautiful is all one can say when they witness the beauty of the Tiger Leaping Gorge. The story behind the name is very interesting as well and sparks curiosity about whether it’s a true fact or not. Visitors can opt to either walk up and down the gorge or purchase tickets to use the escalators. At the end of the trail there’s a nice tourist spot set aside for refreshments and the purchase of souvenirs.

This is the spot where most tourists will visit at Tiger Leaping Gorge. There’s a big parking area for tourists bus here. We visited this place in Nov which is not the peak season (normally in July & Aug when the water level is the highest). Still is a nice place to visit. We paid RMB70 each to take the escalator to and fro to the bottom in order to save time. It’s still pretty crowded even though it’s not in peak season.

Majestic, picturesque, nature at it's best and God's great creation. A journey worth the ride and distance. Take your time to admire and indulge in the beauty while appreciating nature . Don't miss it and it's a must go place .

Visited in April 2024. The weather was quite pleasant, but the windchill is significant. Bring a windbreaker, you will appreciate having it! This place is crowded all year round. We bought escalator tickets for 70RMB. Otherwise you need to descend 800 steps into the gorge, and then climb those 800 steps back up again. There are some souvenir shops, food stalls, and clean public toilets. Watch out for your belongings especially your phone when taking pictures, because people push, and you don't want to lose anything over the side of the railing! Keep your ticket, because you need to scan it a 2nd time to ascend the escalator again at the end of your trip.

This area is between Lijiang and Shangri La in Yunnan. A very scenic gorge to visit and try to go on a day when the weather is good. Place has been developed to be friendly to tourists with walking difficulties as access via 4 levels of escalators is already operational. View is breathtaking and very scenic.

Tiger Leaping Gorge in Yunnan, China, is a breathtaking destination known for its dramatic scenery and adventurous hiking trails. Nestled between Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and Haba Snow Mountain, the gorge is one of the deepest in the world, with a depth of around 3,900 meters1. The Jinsha River roars through the gorge, creating a wild and rugged landscape. Visitors can enjoy stunning views of snow-capped peaks, lush forests, and the powerful river below. The area is also rich in local Naxi culture, adding a unique cultural experience to the natural beauty2. Perfect for nature lovers and adventure seekers!

I did not go to the viewpoint center, but hiked from Upper Gorge to Middle Gorge, ending at Tina's Guesthouse. It was an amazing 2 days hike. Thank goodness it did not rain. Took the bus from Lijiang for 36 yuan. It dropped me off at a location 5 minutes after ticket seller came up the bus. The driver was kind enough to find me a shared car to go up to Naxi Family Guesthouse to start the hike. The shared car pool was 20 yuan per person. The start of the hike was the toughest as it was ascending. After that, the hike was bearable and with great view. Rested for one night near Halfway Guesthouse. Left early in the morning, because I wanted to make sure I got the bus ticket to Shangri-la. Some hikers let the bus driver bring their luggage to Tina's directly. The best view was between Tea Horse Guesthouse and Tina's. After getting my ticket to Shangri-la for 55 yuan, I walked down to the gorge and returned within 3 hours later, for my bus ride. Entrance fees were collected for going down to the gorge, varies between 15 to 30 yuan. To cross the bridge, an extra 10 yuan must be paid.

Tiger Leaping Gorge is a stunning canyon in Yunnan, China, near Lijiang. It is one of the deepest gorges in the world, with the Yangtze River flowing between Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and Haba Snow Mountain. Good place

A very interesting spot as the power of the river running through the narrow gorge is incredible. The main viewing area has stairs (or an esculator) down to several viewing platforms, several with glass decks. I did not do the trek which others have reviewed. The viewing area is crowded most days but worth seeing.

I went on an end March morning. The cold wasn't so bad but the wind was, so take your coat. Essentially the trip consists of walking down 1000 steps, going down a flat walkway for about 20 minutes and then walking up again or taking the escalator. Although I like to walk, the conditions were so uncomfortable that I chose to pay for the escalator up. Go as early as possible to avoid big crowd.

A place most expats in China have probably been to at some point. A truly breathtaking spot which is actually quite easily accessible. This is a hike with astonishing nature, gorgeous views and amazing scenery. It's not a particularly challenging hike either and the route is usually split over two days to make it even easier. The stay over point is aptly named 'Halfway'. If you're lucky and the sky is clear you can get amazing night sky views. Lots of animals roam around here. And the sweeping hills are awe inspiring. Before you start hiking you can check out the raging river if wish but expect tons of people. Bring cash as there's a chance you'll lose your phone signal. And a waterproof coat as the weather can turn quickly

A great little hike that can be done over a few days or a sa 1 day hike down to the river (Tiger Leaping Gorge). Use the 'sky ladder' when you come back up! We visited the river when it was 'calm' and it was still so powerful, god knows what it would be like when in spate? A spectacular area to visit and a must when in the region.
It’s more about the scenic views than anything else. There’s not much here, but if you hike, the experience may be different. If you can’t hike, you can use the escalator, but you’ll have to pay.

Pictures do not do any justice to the awesomeness of Tiger Leaping Gorge. This is a place that has to be experienced in real life. Hiked from Tea Horse guesthouse to Halfway guesthouse and also hiked Middle Gorge. Both are well worth doing.

Truly epic. Well worth doing. We started from Naxi Guesthouse and hiked to Halfway Guesthouse, it took us 6 hours with 2 stops in between. Then after spending a night in a guesthouse head towards Tina’s Guesthouse which is around 2-4 hours more hiking the next day. Then buses will take you to either Lijiang or Shangrila.

Tiger leaping gorge in one day... If you wonder how to do it in one day without sleeping in one of the guesthouses, here is how we did it. Sharing as it wasn't easy to figure out ourselves. We took a driver from Lijiang and asked for a lift to halfway guesthouse, from there we took the beautiful hike high above the canyon with great views down on the river plus waterfalls you can use for refreshing yourself. After 2 hours you will reach Tina guesthouse for a lunch break, then head over the bridge and then down to the middle gorge (this is where the tiger actually jumped as the most narrow spot), it takes half an hour to go down with lots of stairs plus ladders. But down at the waterfront is super impressive and you can take great pics. Then don't go up the same way, you will see a way through the rock which you should take (most people don't do this as both tracks cost 15 yuan each but it is worth it). Then follow the path down to the next village and get up at Sean's guesthouse where your driver should pick you up. We actually missed the trail down to the village and got one up too early which isn't a problem at all as you can walk the last piece on the road. It took us 2 hours to go to Sean's... So in total 4.5 to 5 hours, exhausting due to the climbing up and down but so worth it... Hope that helps many travellers, Jochen

Such an amazing place to visit! Definitely choose the upper trek! Be careful, but if you have some sense in your doings you don’t have any problems to finish the upper trek. Spend first night at Naxi Family House (the best local naxi atmosphere and then another night at tea house or more further.

Tiger Leaping Gorge is known as the most dangerous canyon in the world. Standing on the alley looking down, you can see steep cliffs, deep abyss and swirling water swirling white foam. Very beautiful. Highly recommended ☺️

Beautiful scenery. Many spots to take beautiful pictures. As we’re travelling with elderly and young children, we bought the tickets for the escalator ride down and up. Recommend you buy the enterance ticket and the escalator ticket in advance. Remember to keep your escalator tickets with you for the ride back up. We were visiting in Dec, it was blimey cold with the wind chill factor up. Be sure to be warmly dressed if you’re visiting during the winter months.

If you are coming from Shangri la take the 8 am bus to Tiger Leaping Gorge. It will arrive at 12 noon at Tina Guesthouse Bus Station after a few stops to view the gorge. There is a bus that leaves to Lijiang at 2.30 pm and 3.30 pm. Tina's Guesthouse is good for one nights stay if you prefer

Highly recommend purchasing a ticket for the elevator at Tiger Leaping Gorge for a convenient and worthwhile experience. The views are truly breathtaking, as showcased in my photos and videos. A must-visit for nature enthusiasts!

Tiger Leaping Gorge is, without a doubt, a magnificent natural wonder that fully deserves a visit. The sheer power of the gushing waters and the crashing waves of the river is an exhilarating spectacle. It's truly a soothing and relaxing experience for the soul, and the strong breeze from the gorge is invigorating. ​However, the overall experience is significantly compromised by the truly dreadful state of the public toilets. While trying to fully immerse ourselves in the beautiful scenery and the refreshing river breeze, we were constantly assailed by an incredibly strong stench wafting over from the nearby facilities. It was so unpleasant that it sadly cut our visit short, preventing us from staying as long as we had hoped. ​Go for the incredible natural beauty—you won't be disappointed by the gorge itself—but be prepared for a very unhygienic side note.

Go with a tour guide or private driver is a must. Tour bus OK but rushed. It's like a multibay parking wait to get in with vehicles and pretty difficult without someone who knows how to get in. Off peak OK but peak times expect long entry times lining up in your vehicle
Very nice scenery. The trek isn't too strenuous if you take your time. There are places to stay along the way too. One has a bathroom with the best view ever.

I went hiking there. I spent one and a half days hiking from Lower Tiger Leaping Gorge to Middle Tiger Leaping Gorge. Though the water was not as breathtaking as I thought due to the dry season, the fun and the challenge of the hiking was not disappointing at all. Highly recommended to give it a try.

Hiked this in a solid day and a half. The upper and middle sections of the gorge are beautiful. The lower section is not quite as beautiful, but still worth a visit. The entrance fee as of Dec 2018 dropped to 45RMB, half-price for students like in most places. Would recommend for either a hiking excursion or for a drive through.
It's an easy hike except for the last 10% of the trail where there's a bit of climbing. The views AmaIng
Simply breathtaking. We visited on a sunny afternoon and there are many spots for good photos. We bought the escalator ticket in advanced and things were comfortable.

I spent 4 days hiking through here in 2012 and highly recommend it. Plenty of little homestay/hostels to stay in with resonably priced food and beverage. The hike was extremely interesting with so many different local habitates to experience along the way. Very mountainous terraine with deep valleys and very fast flowing rivers. Fortunately the hiking is quite flat as you do not need to cross any large hills.

It’s rated with AAAA on the rock at the ticket entrance. If you are short of time, just paid 70cny to use the escalator to get to the scenic spot. Opposite across the river, there is a narrow path where the minority tribe used it to transport tea leave to Tibet using the short legged horse 🐎 Just view the posted video

A beautiful canyon surrounded by 5,000m high peaks. We chose to go and hike the trail over 3 days in December 2010 for our Christmas break - and that was freezing cold!! (0C on average) We slept in Naxi's Family guest house and Sean's GH. Both were a relief after hours of walk, we really enjoyed hot showers, soup and heating blankets! The trail is steep at the beginning (the 28 bends) after that it's rather flat and you can find friendly family run guesthouses along the way on average every 3 or 4h of walk. Great memory!
Must see. Road condition is very good for traveling by car or bus. It is also very safe and easy for going down to the river area by escalators.

Beautiful snowcapped mountains to stare in awe of, while hiking through wildflower dotted meadows, and over precarious cliffsides. Extra care must be taken while hiking here, as some passes have become dangerous due to rock slides and erosion. The skyladder is just what your inner adrenaline junkie might be seeking, as if some of the narrow walkways aside a steep descent towards certain death aren't already enough. 😅

Stunning mountains and easier to reach than expected. The bus station close to the South Gate of the ancient town has buses leaving every hour and the bus drivers are happy to help (with a bit of English even :) ) Bring your passport! There is an easy visit to the Gorge with quite a few Chinese tourists or an adventure hike - in either case take your time and enjoy. It's beautiful!

It’s safer to go here with a tour bus cuz the road is super dangerous to drive. NOT RECOMMENDED to drive yourself even u are a very experienced driver. There are tour bus you can access at Lijiang Bus terminal. (Our bus photo attached below) I had the best view here! A bit of hiking once u reach. One of the lifetime experience!!
Amazing view. If u take escalator need to pay 70¥. All Real pics without editing.

This is definitely a worthwhile place to visit if you are having a Trip to Lijiang of Yunnan Province in South West of China .It is about an hour journey by Car from City of Lijiang.We visited in Early September and bought Escalator Tickets (about 800 steps each way if walking )@ Renminbi 70 ( US 10 ) to & fro.View is spectacular .Can be slippery after rain and always crowded.There is a stone in the middle of River which according to Legend Tigers used it as stepping stone to leap across from one side of Gorge to the other which is how the Gorge got its name.Bring a jacket or Umbrella just in case it rains😃😃

One "must" stop at this place while one is at Lijiang or on the way to Shangrila. A deep Gorge with thunderous water pouring into the river. From the top, it's a great hike down into the base of the hill, made easy by the man made steps. Though way down, the journey to view and feel the water and mist, is worth it. View is breathtaking and the feeling is fantastic. Great place for photography too...but the way up, could be a bit strenuous for some. Take a deep breath...
This attraction seems more popular amongst the older generation. It's pretty but it's quite a singular sight. The waterfall is pretty majestic.
A must-go wonderland when you are traveling to Lijiang or Shangri-la. The hike is not too challenging.

Main touristic spot accessible from the small city of Hŭtiàoxiázhèn. The river Jinsha (tributary of the river Yangtze, longest one in Zhōnghuó-China) is tumultuous and impressive. Though it is quite crowded here, mostly to take photos of tiger sculpture. Yes the landscape is beautiful but i suggest to try go a bit deeper in the gorge to see more narrow ways, through dramatic rock walls, falling into the torrent.

Great hike! I took the long route from Qiaotou and while the first day was challenging, I enjoyed it very much. The second half was a less challenging hike with a big part of the route paved. Upside of this was that I could spend more time admiring the views!

Already a lot of people at 9am Although it is a rainy day, the view is gorgeous You can pay extra 70RMB for taking the escalator instead of walking stairs (recommended for rainy days) cuz the stairs are a bit slippery
Good view on the river, it’s impressive Careful the visit doesn’t take that much time (1h max) Cost 45¥ You can book your bus ticket in Lijiang at the main bus station.
Strenuous in the beginning with great views and friendly family run guesthouses along the way. Hardly any traffic in late February and the weather was perfect, consider going in off-season
Be ready with all the stairway going down to visit the Tiger Leaping Gorge. Wasn't visit during peak season and in other words. It wasn't the best to see the spectacular scenes of the rippling waters
No doubt another amazing sight! A must visit destination! Be mindful of your phone! You can choose to walk down for the view or take the escalator (require ticket purchase) 🐯

One word to describe this place - “wow”... near to 1000 steps of staircases to go down to the viewing platform, and climb up too. You can opt to hire people to carry you up and down. RMB150 for one way, RMB200 for two ways.
Surly amazing place to visit. Magnificent mountains, magnificent water, magnificent infrastructure, beautiful people.
I visited the tiger leaping gorge in early April. The weather was pleasantly cool, and not too crowded. It's a majestic canyon.
Definitely will go back for second time if I head back to Lijiang the next time❤️❤️ beautiful trek with decent effort
Visit during non peak season so entry is smooth. It's an amazing place surrounded by nature. Prepared to walk the staircase and not wheelchair friendly.
Had a lifetime experience with fantastic crowd control, multiple elevators for the elderly, guide and most of all seeing the massive torrent of water close up.

during peak season, be prepared to get stuck in traffic just trying to get into the scenic areas. and then you'll have to get off far away and walk in. it's a steep climb down to the river. there were hardly anyone over xmas...
Amazing riverview but I can’t hear a tiger roaring..mybe because its not the high water flow season. Drink hot chocolate for 30yuan 💕🥰 Pay extra 70yuan for the escalator up&down..

We a group of tour 13 persons visit here, only me who go down to take pictures and see the tiger leaping gorge. Hundreds of stair to go down... Go down its easy.. but when you have to climb back... Its really really hard. The oxygen is thin.. every steps are getting heavier. You have to stop several times to rest before you can get to the starting poin. Please bring a bottle of water and dont bring a heavy bag. Please prepare a shirt for change coz when you climb back you will be sweating... And the wind is cold you can catch a cold... Like me hahaha... For older visitor if not has a fit body please reconsider, you can just enjoying the view from the arrival point where there are a lots of bench.
One of the greatest canyon in China. We arrived in motorcycle from Kuala Lumpur.

Need to take multiple steep escalators down. Easy walk. When we were there in early April, the water was not gushing as strong as the videos. The wind was very strong though. Go early and straight to the gorge first as later the crowd will make it impossible to take photos and the locals just refused to move (they take their own sweet time to pose with the tiger statue) and tend to cut queues. We went early (no queue) but took photos along the way to the gorge. By the time we reached the tiger statue, it was already so crowded. Don’t be trick by the FREE photo is so small like 1.5 cm that you can’t even see your face clearly. Next thing they make you pay for the bigger one upstairs. Nothing spectacular about the place unless you hike.
Spectacular, worth the climb down and up the 200 over steps. The deepest gorge River in the world.

An absolutely fantastic experience to be right next to the raging Yangtze River when it gushes through the narrow gorge. While you need to walk several stairs down from the car park to reach the level of the river you will experience a fascinating natural spectacle. Worthwhile every step of the way.

I did the Tiger Leaping Gorge upper trail. There are locals that sell drinks and fruits everywhere along the trail. The trail is fine till the Half-way inn, which is way past halfway of the trail. I would take the shuttle bus to Tina's guest house if you aren't experienced. Because after the Halfway inn the descending begins. The paths are very narrow, there lots of mountain goats and there are no rails that protect you from falling. Also there are loose stones and it's very slippery. At one point you have to cross a stream of water which is really dangerous, which comes from the waterfall shown in the map. I would recommend this trail to experienced hikers. However the view was beautiful, even though I was mostly focussed on not falling to my death. It took me 8 hours to finish this trail and I took quite a lot of breaks.

Absolutely a must visit site. The gorge constrict the Jiangsha river causing magnificent rushing rapids. There are two ways down the gorge -the stairways or the faster escalators. A long platform along the river bank allow for safe sight seeing.

We had two day trek here and it was simply amazing. We took bus from Lijiang around 9am and reached the start of the trek around noon. We paid the fee for entering the park and head to the trail. First few kilometres are hard because you have to climb up but it is definitely worth it. We slept at Tea-house guest house and continue next day to Tina's guest house from where we too bus. The trek is simply amazing and worth of the effort.

Stopped by here on the way to Shangrila. I shall not even attempt to describe the beauty and magnificence of what I saw. Documentaries, Youtube Videos nor Photos can do any justice! So i'll just say that it is a sight that you will need to see with your own eyes and to hear the thunderous roar with your own ears. As you take deep breaths of the crisp fresh air.. there is no need to touch the raging torrent to fathom its force, you can feel it reverberating deep in your bones... totally spellbound by its sheer power! Ignoring the only downside... the crowd, the Tiger Leaping Gorge is super picturesque, super spectacular, super accessible.... no climbing, abseiling or treking.... its a few sets of modern escalators all the way down to the viewing area!

A spectacular journey. Unforgettable. Not to be missed. We did a two day hike. If you get the chance to do it, do not hesitate. You don't have to be in peak physical condition, but you have to be ready to hike about 20 miles at high altitude with pretty rudimentary accommodations. Well worth the minor hardships though!!!!

A powerful River that you can strongly feel the Mother Nature. It will be a hiking trip here. If you’re lazy, there is also the elevator choice. Quite crowded, but there’s no need to worry about the parking spot. Park your car by following the guidance, and enjoy the river. It might be the most popular spot of Jinsha River.

Incredible nature down there. The path down was constructed by locals and was a real experience. One should know that the path is very narrow and not overly secured. Recommended for fitte people who are not afraid of heights. The force of the river itself was incredible and the water seemed to boil. Sadly due to pollution the water is brown/grey.

Beautiful in august when its raining and huge water mass is hitting this gorge. Well maintained .lot of stairs..worth going. But major issue is traffic jam and management due to huge number of car influx...it took three hours to go 6 km during August.. Worth probably after that..

Tiger Leaping Gorge is situated on the Yangtze River in southwestern China. About 15 km (9 miles) in length, the canyon passes through a series of rapids surrounded by mountains on both sides that sharply rise 3,000 meters (10,000 feet) above the river. It is believed to be the deepest canyon in the world – depending on the criteria applied. The hiking trail through the gorge is one of the most accessible and satisfying in China, with dramatic scenery. The hike is not to be taken lightly though. Even for those in good physical shape, it’s a workout and can certainly wreck the knees. Accommodation along the way is in guesthouses, so hikers won’t need a tent.
Amazing place!!can't say by words spectacular water streaming with tremenous sound. What can I say, WOW!!
Nature is really spectacular, this is the stream of Changjiang River - Jinsha River.

This is a Shangri-La area attraction that should not be missed. The views are amazing in this 3900 meter deep gorge along the Yangtze River. It's a lot of exercise with lots of steps down and back up again. If the stairs are a problem for you, you can get a ride in a carry cart for 200 RMB.

Tiger Leaping Gorge is located in the north of China's Yunnan province. It is one of the deepest gorges in the world, with a depth of 3900 m and a length of 16 km, sandwiched between the snowy mountains of Haba Shan in the west and Yulong Xueshan in the east. According to legend, here the tiger ran away from the hunters and jumped over the stormy river in the narrowest place with a large stone in the middle, which gave the name to the gorge. The Golden Sands River (as the Yangtze is called in this area) forms whole cascades of rapids here. They are quite dangerous to pass, but this does not stop rafting enthusiasts. In 1986, the rapids of the river were conquered for the first time.
worth to visit Suitable for novice hiker Must go places Nice accommodation Nice food Nice view Magnificent view

If you are thinking of hiking in Tibet China, consider the Tiger Leaping Gorge. We flew from Singapore to Chengdu to Lijiang. We stayed in the Banyan Tree Lijiang for 2 nights. From there it was just a 1.5 hour ride to the entry of the Gorge. The 17km trail through the Tiger Leaping Gorge is considered one of the best hikes in the world. It swirls through a canyon created by the majestic Yangtze River with spectacular views of towering Himalayan peaks with names like Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and Haba Snow Mountain. We completed the hike in one day. We started at the Naxi village (2100m) at 09:30am. From there 28 bends took us to the highest point at (2650m). That is a 1 hour walk, which we did at quite a steady pace. It was quite though. It is steep and the height did it's work on our lungs. On the top we had beautiful views over the gorge. Very rewarding. And there was a nice lady selling water and bananas. From there it is another 1.5hour decent to Tea Horse Trade Guest House. And 1.5 hour more to Halfway Guest House. From 13:30 to 14:30 we had lunch at Halfway. The fried eggs were delicious and the Tsingtao topped it off completely on the sun deck overlooking the snowy mountains. From Halfway to Tina's Guest House it is another 1.5 hour. We reached there at 4pm, where our driver was waiting to take us back to the Banyan Tree. This was a wonderful day and the hike comes highly recommended.
The waters are fierce, legend says a tiger leapt across the gorge despite the raging river flow
One of my favorite places in china and one of the best hikes in the world. The trails are very well prepared and there are plenty hostel options available.

The most famous place in the Lijiang area is the tiger leaping channel (Hu tiao Xia). For tourists who want to reach only this point, you can drive to the beginning of the new path parallel to the river, 500 steps down the concrete steps where you can descend to a stormy waterfall , Almost to the water. Those who have trouble walking can walk this path with the help of porters who take the hard ones on chairs. For those who are looking for trekking: "The length of the gorge is about 16 kilometers, and it stretches between the villages of Da ju and Qiao tou.Tao has to choose between a number of tracks: the long and hard trail (about thirty kilometers, ), The lower path, which is a relatively convenient one-day road, and a new, easy trail (about an hour). The first day on the upper trail begins with a five- to seven-hour walk, which includes a steep climb up a winding path, a more moderate climb, crossing the ridge, descending and continuing on a flat track. From there they walk for another two hours to Walnut Grove, where they stay in the Half Way inn or elsewhere. On the second day you go down to the ravine for about four hours, cross the river by ferry and arrive at De Dezou in about two hours (you can also give up the Dezou and return to the beginning of the runway on the lower, lighter trail). "

It is fairly impressive, but probably the most overrated sight in China and not really worth the effort in my view. If you read Lonely Planet and the rest of them they make it out to be the Grand Canyon, but it isn’t.

Breathtaking view along the trekking path. It was a two days one night trek started from Qiaotou town which is 2 hours driving distance away from Lijing city centre. It was a sunny day when we did the trek, and it is highly recommended that you bring along some sunscreen to avoid sunburn. You can buy snacks and water at certain points of the trek but everything is a little bit more expensive here. The first day we spent 8.5 hours to go from Qiaotou Town to Halfway Hostel. And for the second day it was another 2 hours trek from Halfway Hostel to Tina guesthouse, where we pick up our main luggage and depart to Lijiang from
Very beautiful and definetly worth visiting if you're already in the region. Though nowadays one has to pay to enter and it's quite touristic.
Beautiful place if you don’t mind geographically area that different than usual look. But have lots of steps to go down and to see that view. Avoid the holiday season in china
There is a small trail we take down in the middle of the gorge. My 5 year old is able to do the hike, but he is quite fit.
In 2014, We rode from Malaysia to Lijiang by a motorcycle. Due to bad weather and the road is slippery, we have to continues by a car. It's amazing place. Worth to reached here
Worth visiting to admire the powerful river. Can you spot the tiger statue on the other side of the river? A lot of stairs to go down to the river, but worth it.
Cool place but mind your step. It does get a little crowded and is quite steep. If your too tired you can be carried for a fee.
It's great to visit this after raining. But please prepare to walk ups and downs. Or you can pay ¥200 for someone to take you down and up.
If I have to pick one from this and the White Water Terrace, I'd definitely pick the later.
Top rated thrill with water rushing past you .You can feel the movement in your body
Very impressive, If you come by coach, you will probably have the option to either stop at the first spot, either at the second one. The second one is muuuuuuch more impressive !!
Some master swordsman told me in my dream, it's the place where The Legend of Condor Heroes came from...

reviews.text: เป็นสถานที่ที่เดินชายฝั่งริมน้ำในช่องแคบภูเขา สวยงามมาก ลมแรงมาก หนาวมาก ลึกมาก มีทั้งแบบเดินเองและใช้บันไดเลื่อนซึ่งเราใช้บันไดเลื่อน เพราะจะเสียเวลาเดินมากและเหนื่อย เราจะเดินทางต่อไปอีก

Tiger Leaping Gorge " ialah ngarai dalam yang menakjubkan di Sungai Jinsha di Yunnan, China. terletak di utara Bandar Lama Lijiang, antara "Jade Dragon Snow Mountain" dan "Haba Snow Mountain ", Ia adalah salah satu gaung terdalam di dunia, menampilkan jeram yang dramatik, arus deru dan pemandangan popular yang menakjubkan dan tinggi. Menurut legenda tempatan, seekor harimau melompat menyeberangi sungai yang sempit di bahagian tertentu gaung itu untuk melarikan diri daripada pemburu — sebab itu dinamakan “Tiger Leaping Gorge” 🐅

세계 최대 협곡답게 웅장하고 압도적인 풍광. 비가 많이 온 이후라서 협곡물이 무섭게 흐름. 미국의 그랜드캐년과 비교를 할 수 없는 절경임. 옥룡설산과 하바설산 사이에 협곡. 트래킹 코스가 중간 난이도 정도로 젊은 나이(대학생정도임)의 중국인들이 아주 많이 보임 트래킹 중에 간간히 옥룡설산의 13개 봉우리가 보임 (맑은 날씨보다는 흐린날이 트래킹 하기에 적합해보임)

พอลงจากลานจอดรถ เดินลงบันไดมาประมาณ 100 กว่าขั้น สำหรับใครที่ซื้อตั๋วลงบันไดเลื่อนมา ก็สามารถยื่นตั๋วให้กับเจ้าหน้าที่ ลงบันไดเลื่อนมาทั้งหมดสี่ตอนด้วยกัน แล้วก็ลง มาเรื่อยๆจนเดินสุดท้ายได้ชมความงามของช่องแคบเสือกระโจน เวลาหน้าหนาวลมแรงแล้วก็หนาวมาก แต่ถ้ามีแดดแดดก็แรงมากเช่นเดียวกัน เตรียมแว่นตากันแดดแล้วก็หมวกแล้วก็เสื้อกันหนาวมาให้พร้อม
ต้องเดินลงไปลึกมาก แต่มีบันไดเลื่อนที่ทอดยาวลงไปสามชั้น ช่วยให้ขึ้นลงได้สะดวก ซื้อตั๋วราคา 70 หยวน
虎跳峽真的超壯觀！遊客也非常多，山谷超深，江水聲音很震撼，走在步道上就能感受到大自然的力量。路程雖然有一點挑戰，不過沿途風景值得慢慢走、慢慢看。建議穿好走的鞋子，也可以帶點水跟小零食。整體來說非常值得一來，算是麗江必去的景點之一
Nên mua vé đi thang cuốn 380 tệ vì thang lên xuống rất dốc, mệt nếu leo cầu thang, cảnh đẹp

Pastikan kamu turun menggunakan eskalator. Pengalaman yang menyenangkan melihat legenda tiger Leaping Jorge ini. Ini merupakan perbatasan dari lijiang dan Shangrila. Tetap disisi satunya sepi Ini merupakan legenda seekor harimau yang dikejar pemburu dan melompati sungai yang sangat deras demi bisa selamat dari kejaran pemburu
2025/8/10 携程旅行で麗江-虎跳峡間往復134元のツアーバスを予約し訪問。 乗車場所は複数あり指定できる。 茶馬客桟→老師客桟は3時間弱 性根逞しく売店やトイレ(1-2元 QR決済)は至る所にあり装備は軽装でOK 崖っぷちを歩いたり、眼下に見える金沙江を眺めたりと最高にいい景色。 途中、洗越えが1箇所あるので防水の靴はあったほうがよいかも。
호도협을 보기 위해 에스컬레이터를 타고 내려가 둘러보고 다시 올라와 차를 타고 이동한 후 2시간 정도 트레킹을 했다. 멀리 옥룡설산이 보이는 협곡 트레킹 -- 잊지 못 할 추억!

🌄 Hổ Khiêu Hiệp Một điểm tham quan thiên nhiên hùng vĩ, dễ đi mà không cần trekking. Đường vào có lối đi bộ, thang cuốn, phù hợp cả người già và trẻ nhỏ. 🎟️ Giá vé: hơi cao nếu bạn không muốn đi bộ có thể mua thêm vé thang cuốn 70 tệ 🕘 Tham quan: mất khoảng 1–2 giờ. Có quán nước, WC và chỗ nghỉ chân dọc đường. 📝 Lưu ý: nên đi vào mùa khô, mang giày thoải mái, đồ nhẹ. Sáng sớm hoặc chiều là thời điểm chụp hình đẹp nhất. (Mình đi trưa nắng tung đầu) ✅ Rất đáng để ghé nếu bạn yêu thiên nhiên và muốn ngắm sông Kim Sa giữa núi tuyết Ngọc Long – Haba mà không cần trekking nặng.

虎跳峽，這名字一聽就很狂，親眼見到更是氣勢驚人—— 站在峽谷邊緣，我真的有一瞬間懷疑自己是不是站在大自然的怒吼前面。 這裡位於金沙江，是長江的上游，尤其在雨季來時，那水流根本不是「流」，是「衝」、「炸」、「咆哮」！ 我一邊扶著欄杆，一邊想：「如果我是一隻老虎，看到這麼猛的水，也真會跳。」🐯（雖然更可能是被沖走） 水濺起來像霧，風夾著水氣直往臉上打，像是大自然親自給我來個免費去角質洗臉SPA， 眼前的每一秒都在上演驚心動魄的現場直播，完全不需要音效剪輯，轟隆隆的聲音就像在耳邊開重低音演唱會。 走過那幾段木棧道，心裡真的會浮現一句話：「人類啊，你真渺小。」 但同時，也覺得自己好幸運，能夠在滾滾江水與峽谷之間，目睹這場天地共鳴的奇景。 總之，虎跳峽不是來拍網美照的地方， 是來感受什麼叫「水可以吼出聲音」、什麼叫「大自然不需要修圖」的地方。

🏔️ ช่องแคบเสือกระโจน (Tiger Leaping Gorge) 🐅 . สถานที่ท่องเที่ยวได้รับขึ้นทะเบียนเป็นมรดกโลก UNESCO ตั้งอยู่ในมณฑลยูนนาน ประเทศจีน 🇨🇳 . ที่นี่เป็นหุบเขาลึก มีน้ำไหลเชี่ยว และ วิวภูเขาใหญ่ตระการตา ช่องหุบเขานี้มีความยาว 15 กิโลเมตร ตำแหน่งที่ตั้งอยู่ในบริเวณที่แม่น้ำไหลผ่านระหว่าง ภูเขาหิมะมังกรหยก และ ภูเขาหิมะฮาป๋า ซึ่งเป็นบริเวณที่น้ำไหลเชี่ยวและอยู่ใต้หน้าผาสูง 2,000 เมตร ซึ่งตามตำนานกล่าวว่า มีเสือตัวหนึ่งได้หนีการตามล่าจากนายพราน โดยกระโดดข้ามแม่น้ำที่จุดที่แคบที่สุด กว้าง 25 เมตร จึงเป็นที่มาของชื่อ “ช่องแคบเสือกระโจน” 🐅
4月初，從麗江前往香格里拉的路上，遊歷虎跳峽。 介於玉龍雪山和哈巴雪山中間金沙江水，受两岸高山的緊緊束缚，江流入峡後，最窄處虎豹一躍而起，故名虎跳峡。 除了可以走木棧道到江邊，另有付費70元人民幣的手扶梯可搭，觀景台皆設有打卡照相裝置藝術，很好拍。 我為江水波濤洶湧感到震撼，驚心動魄！回頭一看，牆上掛著「只要熱愛生命，一切皆有可能」警語😅

Magnifique paysage ! Une randonnée accessible d’environ 10km est possible (High trail). Il faut demander à votre hôtel un minibus pour le trajet aller/retour (on a payé 180 yuans) et vous dépose au Tee Horse Guesthouse pour vous récupérer à Zang Teacher Guesthouse. Les horaires sont souvent 8h pour le départ de Lijiang et 15h30 pour le retour. Je recommande ! En cette période (janvier) nous n’avons pas payé d’entrée mais nous n’avons pas eu accès au bordure de la rivière.
Wunderbare Wandertouren über mehrere Tage möglich! Es ist sehr ruhig und nach spätestens 3,5 Stunden kommt ein Punkt, um sich mit einem Sammeltaxi abholen zu lassen, falls man will.

ช่องเขาที่ลึกและแคบที่สุดช่วงหนึ่งของสาขาหนึ่งของแม่น้ำแยงซีเกียง จากสายน้ำสีเขียวนิ่งๆ (ในช่วงฤดูใบไม้ผลิ) พอไหลผ่านชองเขาแคบๆ ทำให้เกิดน้ำไหลเชี่ยวรุนแรง เสียงดังกระหึ่ม กับภาพบรรยากาศที่เป็นเทือกเขาสูงรอบด้าน ทำให้เกิดวิวที่สวยงามมากยิ่งขึ้น การเข้าชมต้องซื้อตั๋วก่อน และจากลานจอดรถ จะมีบันได้เลื่อนประมาณ 3-4 ช่วง นำลงไปยังริมแม่น้ำ ระหว่างทาง จะเห็นจุดชมวิวสวยๆตลอดทาง จนกระทั่งถึงด้านล่างก็จะมีทางเดินเลียบแม่น้ำไปยังจุดที่แคบที่สุด จนมีเรื่องเล่าว่า เสือสามารถกระโดดข้ามได้ เป็นที่มาของชื่อสถานที่แห่งนี้ จนสุุดทางจะมีจุดชมวิว และรูปปั้นเสือเหลียวหลังเป็นสัญลักษณ์ให้ถ่ายรูป และใกล้ๆกันจะมีร้านขายป้ายให้เขียนคำขอพร แล้วแขวนไว้ ซึ่งมีป้ายแขวนไว้อยู่เป็นจำนวนมาก ถ่ายรูปได้สวยอีกมุม นักท่องเที่ยวชาวจีนจำนวนมาก ต้องพยายามแทรกหามุมเพื่อให้ได้รูปสวยๆ ก็สนุกไปอีกแบบ ที่นี่เป็นแหล่งท่องเที่ยวระดับ AAAAA และมรดกโลกด้วย

Aquí va la informació que m'hagués agradat tenir sobre la ruta que va de les 28 curves fins a Tina GH. En primer lloc, no et preocupis per arribar-hi. Desde Shangri-La i Lijiang trobaràs diversos busos i el teu hostel et pot ajudar. La ruta és fàcil per a qualsevol persona amb una mica de forma física i que hagi fet alguna cosa de muntanya a la seva vida. En total han estat 16 km i 700 m de desnivell. No t'has de preocupar per la logística perquè hi ha parades de menjar cada 500 m i molta gent fent el camí. Porta unes bones sabates, roba adecuada i una mica d'aigua. Podràs menjar a mig camí, nosaltres ho vam fer a TeaHorse GH (arròs amb carn per 40 Yuan). Tot i que la ruta es pot fer en un dia, nosaltres vam decidir parar a dormir a un dels hotels de mig camí. Recomano fer-ho per viure la ruta amb calma i disfrutar les vistes més temps. El paisatge és impressionant i això no s'ho poden carregar, del tot. Però si el que busques és naturalesa verge, aventura, sentir-te aïllat... Oblida't-en. Pel camí et trobes construccions, cablejat elèctric, tubs d'aigua i molta brutícia, plàstic per tot arreu. No ha sigut el trekking èpic que ens imaginàvem, però si saps al que vens... No deixa de valdre la pena.
雲南香格里拉長江上游金沙江, 江水一直流向到最窄江口~ 虎跳峽, 江水澎湃洶湧. 非常壯觀, 是旅遊必到打卡位. 香格里拉是一高源地區, 山勢峻嶺, 十分獨特.
2025-3-23 - 3月份，水位比较低，但河水漂亮 - 传说中的虎跳石，稳稳屹立在水中 - 水流很急，风很大，峡谷风景很美 - 游客可以选择“走楼梯”上下峡谷 或 付费 搭“自动扶梯”上下峡谷， 无论如何，有一些路必须要走楼梯

香格里拉虎跳峡Tiger Leaping Gorge Scenic Spot。感恩能一睹那惊心动魄的绝壁急流、感受水的汹涌澎湃，心灵震撼看了如此壮观的峡谷。 位于云南省迪庆藏族自治州香格里拉市虎跳峡镇和丽江市玉龙县龙蟠乡境内的金沙江上，是世界上最深最窄的大峡谷之一、中国最美十大峡谷之一。南岸为玉龙雪山，北岸为哈巴雪山。江流入峡后宽仅50多米，最窄处虎豹一跃即过，故名虎跳峡。虎跳峡的最大特点就是它的落差。从上虎跳到下虎跳，落差213米，江流湍急，江水从高处奔腾而下，形成了一幅极其震撼的画面。站在峡谷的观景台上，只见近白的江水湍急而狂野，奔流不息般向下冲刷。水流迅猛而汹涌，凶猛地冲击着江中屹立的虎跳石，水花四溅，惊涛拍岸，卷起千层浪，洒落飞花无数，仿佛与天地相连，奏响了一曲与命运抗争的交响曲！亲身体验这样的景象，令人畏惧，震摄心灵。

리장에서 새벽에 출발해서 나시객잔에서 시작해서 중도객잔에서 하루 숙박하고 티나객잔으로 하산하는 1박2일 트래킹을 했어요. 교통편은 리장여행사에 합류해서 편하게 할수 있었어요. 새로 짓는 숙소들이 많아서 현대식으로 편하게 숙박할수 있었어요. 28벤드를 올라가는것이 부담스러우면 나시객잔에서 말을 타고 올라가는 방법도 있습니다. 표지판이 잘되어 있어서 길헤맬일은 없지만 차마객잔과 중도객잔을 떠날때는 표식판찾기 어려울수 있어요. 마지막구간은 Tina's Guesthouse 이정표를 따라가면 쉽습니다. 유튜브 허여사의 여행일기에 편집해서 올렸으니 참고하세요

徒步的虎跳峽令人驚豔，靠水而行時可感受澎湃的水聲，靠山而行時可感受山景的秀麗，可依自己的腳力選擇不同的路程，有機會想再回去走一趟。 一段回憶記錄文字 虎跳峽本不在雲南麗江的行程之中，但在麗江古城閒晃2日後有點發荒，剛好入住的『麗江國際青年旅社』的櫃台可以協助訂麗江往中虎跳峽的巴士票，想說去看看名滿中國的長江第一峽虎跳的的氣勢磅礡，也順便走一小段中虎跳的徒步路線。 從麗江古城到虎跳峽車程約需3小時，不想讓行程過於匆忙，在巴士終點站的『中峽國際青年旅舍』（Tina's YHA）訂了一晚的住宿。安排好車票與住宿，隔日早上帶著簡便的行李，7:40從麗江搭小巴出發，到達香格里拉上虎跳風景區入口時，巴士暫停下來，接著有景區工作人員上車跟車上人員收取門票費用，需購買65RMB[2016年6月票價]的景區門票才能進入。進入景區後，巴士上的人依徒步天數的不同，會請司機師傅在登山口附近停車，隨著接近虎跳中段，車上的人也遇來遇少。雖然是直達巴士，但經過上虎跳峽景區，司機師父還是會停10分鐘，讓車上的人看一下被玉龍與哈巴雪山所夾擊而成的天下第一峽，的確是水聲驚人，但可惜在水上漂浮不少垃圾，原本磅礴的景色也頓時遜色，不免為之可惜。 巴士在11:00前到達Tina's YHA，放下行李後直接請旅舍送我到中虎跳徒步入口。徒步路線據說是當地人自我維護，全程共有2段要收費，第一段10RMB，收錢的方式也挺特別的，在下車的地點往下走時，突然從旁邊出現一位身穿傳統服飾的老婆婆擆著拐杖出現，也沒說話只是伸出手，詢問她是要收過路費嗎？婆婆點頭稱是，於是付了10RMB往下走，徒步路線很清楚也很平坦好走，路線隨著金沙江而行。步行一陣子後，看到一柵鐡門即是第二段收費路程，一位少女過來收取15RMB的費用並同時給了一張收據。這段路程有一些村民修建的吊穚可讓走向河中央的大石，站在石上可以直接感受金沙江的沖刷力道，挺有野趣，只是這些穚都是私自圈地而蓋，要走上穚都要收費10-15RMB不等。 第一段徒步是由上而下，接下來都是平坦直行，到第二段後半則開始由下而上，對於體力則開始有小小考驗，特別是有一段垂直90度的天梯過程也考驗著膽量。往上走的過程會經過山間的小舖，是由幾根木頭簡單搭建而成，當然物價貴了不少，但突然想喝冰飲時也是個歇腿的選擇，接著再堅持往上走就可抵達Tina's YHA下方的馬路。
往香格里拉的路途中，一定會經過景點，虎跳峽。 非常壯觀的滔滔江水，虎跳峽位於麗江與香格里拉的交界、玉龍與中甸間的金沙江幹流上，以「深、險、奇、絕、秀」的曠世景觀而出名，也是世界上最深的峽谷之一；兩岸的兩座雪山分別為玉龍雪山及哈巴雪山～

虎跳峽是中國雲南省麗江一處峽谷，位於玉龍與中甸之間的金沙江幹流上。相傳金沙江逢枯水期時，有猛虎下山，在此江中的礁石上稍一腳後騰空便越過，故稱「虎跳峽」，江中的礁石則稱作「虎跳石」。 虎跳峽的兩岸有雪山對峙，左岸（西面）為哈巴雪山，右岸（東面）為玉龍雪山，自谷底到山頂高差達3790米。虎跳峽全長約16公里，分成上虎跳、中虎跳、下虎跳三段，始於金沙江及其支流碩多崗河匯合處，即中甸縣橋頭鎮一帶；止於玉龍縣大具鄉一帶。虎跳峽兩側岩石為片岩和大理岩組成，寬度僅60至80米，最窄處約30餘米，天然落差200多米，水流湍急，水力資源蘊藏豐富。

虎跳峡虽然离丽江更近，但是他是属于迪庆藏族自治州管辖范围内。车先开到了售票点，每家派一人前去买票，我们到的时候还很早，没几个人，等回来的时候发现这里已经排起了长队，司机说，人多的时候光买票就要排2小时，然后进入虎跳峡景区的道路又非常狭窄，都是双向一车道的路，国庆假日在这里光堵车就能堵好几个小时。 我们到达景区的时候发现，这里人已经非常多了，虎跳峡是我们云南行中去的唯一一个旅游点，其实十几年前我们已经来过一次，这次正好是7月雨季，想让女儿来这里感受下虎跳峡的气势。

Hổ Khiêu Hiệp hay còn gọi Khe Hổ Nhảy (虎跳峡) dài khoảng 15 km và có độ cao tối đa 3790m. Hổ Khiêu Hiệp nằm ở đầu nguồn sông Dương Tử, con sông dài thứ ba trên thế giới và là con sông quan trọng nhất ở Trung Quốc. Hổ Khiêu Hiệp được chia thành 3 đoạn gọi là: hẻm trên, hẻm giữa và hẻm dưới. Toàn bộ thung lũng dài khoảng 18 km theo hướng từ tây nam sang đông bắc. Nó nằm giữa Hutiaoxia Zhen (虎跳峡镇 /Tiger Leaping Gorge Town) gần hẻm núi trên và thị trấn Daj(大具乡) gần hẻm núi Lower. Cái tên hẻm núi Hổ bắt nguồn từ một câu chuyện kể xa xưa. Một thợ săn đang đuổi theo một con hổ qua hẻm núi, khi đến điểm hẹp nhất, con hổ nhảy qua sông Jinsha, thoát khỏi người thợ săn. Hòn đá nơi con hổ thực hiện cú nhảy của nó giờ là một điểm nhìn mang tính biểu tượng và hẻm núi được đặt tên theo con hổ.

La randonnée est vraiment superbe ! Tout d’abord je vous conseille de démarrer celle-ci à la Naxi GuestHouse et non à l’entrée du parc. En effet l’entrée du parc est ravagée par la construction de 2 ponts géants. Depuis Naxi GH, il vous faudra 5h30 de marche (pause déjeuner incluse) pour atteindre Tina Guesthouse, comptez 20 minutes de plus pour rejoindre Tibetan Guesthouse. Si vous avez déjà effectué des randonnées et que vous êtes en bonne santé celle-ci n’est pas difficile : environ 600/700 mètres de dénivelé. Les fameux 28 lacets n’ont rien d’insurmontable même si forcément vous allez transpirer :) Dans cette configuration, la randonnée s’effectue en une journée. Vous pouvez aussi continuer vers Ennu Village, mais prévoyez 1 jour supplémentaire. Si vous souhaitez descendre dans les gorges ( au pied de la rivière) depuis Tina Guesthouse, il faudra donner 15 RMB. 20 minutes pour descendre et 40 minutes pour remonter. Enfin, nous avons réalisé la randonnée début décembre : aucun signe d’enneigement, il faisait environ 15 degrés en pleine journée. PS : j’ai joint le plan photographié sur place, mais gardez à l’esprit que les temps indiqués sont vraiment larges.

Tiger Leaping Gorge nằm ở phía bắc tỉnh Vân Nam, Trung Quốc. Đây là một trong những hẻm núi sâu nhất thế giới, với độ sâu 3900 m và chiều dài 16 km, nằm giữa dãy núi tuyết Haba Shan ở phía tây và Yulong Xueshan ở phía đông. Theo truyền thuyết, tại đây, con hổ đã chạy trốn khỏi những người thợ săn và nhảy qua dòng sông giông bão ở nơi hẹp nhất với một tảng đá lớn ở giữa, nơi đặt tên cho hẻm núi. Sông Golden Sands (như Dương Tử được gọi trong khu vực này) tạo thành toàn bộ thác ghềnh ở đây. Chúng khá nguy hiểm để vượt qua, nhưng điều này không ngăn được những người đam mê đi bè. 虎跳峡镇，是中华人民共和国云南省迪庆藏族自治州香格里拉市下辖的一个乡镇级行政单位.儅人們從云南崐明出發到香格裏拉，虎跳峽是必經之地，這裏的景色宜人，還能遠遠眺望到玉籠雪山。在陽光白云，青山綠水的襯托下，顯的分外妖嬈，值得一去！ Tiger Leaping Gorge Town is a township-level administrative unit under the jurisdiction of Shangri-La City, Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, People's Republic of China. When people set out from Kunming, Yunnan to Shangri-La, Tiger Leaping Gorge is a must-go place. The scenery here is pleasant, You can also see Yulong Snow Mountain from a distance. Against the backdrop of sunshine, white clouds, and green mountains and rivers, it is extremely enchanting and worth visiting!

호도협 - 호랑이가 건너다니던 협곡으로 가는 길 위룽쉐산과 하바쉐산을 끼고 이어지는 16km의 협곡. 윈난성의 차를 싣고 티베트로 가던 마방들의 자취를 따라가는, 실크로드보다 오래된 옛길. 옥빛 금사강의 물길을 따라, 흰빛 설산에 기대어 세계에서 가장 깊은 협곡으로 들어가는 길. 하나의 나라라고 하기에는 너무나 다양한 얼굴을 지닌 중국. 거대한 대륙 중국의 서남쪽에 자리 잡은 윈난성은 중국을 구성하는 55개 소수부족 중 26개의 소수부족이 살고 있는 인문학적 환경과 다양한 자연환경으로 세계인을 매료시켜왔다. 그런 윈난성이 품고 있는 보물 같은 트레킹 루트가 바로 호도협(虎跳峽)이다. 세계에서 가장 긴 강 장강(長江)이 이곳에 오면 '금사강'으로 이름을 바꾸고 거대한 두 산의 발치로 접어든다. 인도 대륙과 유라시아 대륙의 충돌로 야기된 지각운동은 하나였던 산을 위룽쉐산(玉龍雪山, 5,596m)과 하바쉐산(哈巴雪山, 5,396m)으로 갈라놓았다. 그 갈라진 틈으로 장강(長江)이 흘러들면서 16km의 길이에 높이 2,000m에 달하는 길고 거대한 협곡이 만들어졌다. 가장 험하고 아름다운 구간 이 협곡의 길은 먼 옛날부터 차마고도(茶馬古道)의 일부로 불려왔다. 차마고도는 실크로드보다 오래된 교역로로, 중국 당나라와 티베트 토번 왕국이 차와 말을 교역하던 데서 이름이 유래했다. 중국의 서남부 윈난성과 쓰촨성에서 티베트를 넘어 네팔과 인도까지 이어지는 5,000km의 길에서 가장 험하고 아름다운 구간이 산장빙류(三江并流) 협곡이다. 금사강(金沙江 장강의 상류), 난창강(瀾滄江 메콩강의 상류), 누강(怒江 살윈강의 상류)이 횡단산맥의 5,000m 이상의 설산 사이로 흘러간다. 협곡을 따라가는 평균 해발고도 4,000m가 넘는 험준한 길의 지형적 특이함과 세계의 동물 중 25퍼센트가 존재하는 생물학적 다양성으로 인해 세계자연유산으로 지정되었다. 윈난성에서 티베트로 향하는 차마고도는 시솽반나(西雙版納)에서 푸얼스(普耳市)를 지나 따리(大理), 리장(麗江), 상거리라(香格里拉)를 거쳐 라싸(拉薩)에 이르는데 리장에서 샹그릴라로 향하는 길목에 호도협이 자리 잡고 있다. 호랑이가 건너다닌 협곡이라는 뜻의 호도협은 강의 상류와 하류 낙차가 170m에 이른다. 세계에서 가장 깊은 협곡 중의 하나다
